issues.title: Tailwind classes in incorrect order
issues.description: Tailwind utility classes must follow standard ordering: layout, positioning, sizing, spacing (margin before padding), typography, visual effects. The classes have padding (pr-2) before margin (mt-[-16px]), which violates this convention.
issues.rule_name: Tailwind CSS Classes Must Follow Standard Ordering

issues.title: Missing optional chaining causes runtime error when openForm is undefined
issues.description: The code accesses `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but openForm can be undefined when rendering certain forms (like the main comment form). The original code correctly used `openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet` with optional chaining. This will cause a "Cannot read property 'in_reply_to_snippet' of undefined" runtime error when the FormWrapper is rendered without an openForm prop, crashing the component.

issues.title: Editor editability incorrectly depends on member expertise instead of name
issues.description: The Form component determines whether the editor should be editable by checking `member?.expertise` instead of `memberName` (which is derived from `member?.name`). According to the comment and the original logic, the editor should be disabled only when the member doesn't have a name or when submitting. Expertise is optional metadata, but name is required for posting. This bug prevents users without expertise from typing in the comment editor, even though they have a valid name and should be allowed to comment.

issues.title: Reply threading broken for nested comments due to incorrect in_reply_to_id
issues.description: The submit function uses `parent.id` as `in_reply_to_id` instead of `openForm.in_reply_to_id`. For nested replies (replying to a reply), these values differ: `openForm.in_reply_to_id` points to the specific comment being replied to, while `parent.id` points to the top-level parent comment. Using `parent.id` breaks the reply chain, causing nested replies to be incorrectly threaded to the wrong comment. This destroys the conversation hierarchy and makes it impossible to track which comment a user is actually replying to in multi-level discussions.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25858 - Fixed reply form showing parent comment author's details

structured_output.summary:
The PR fixes a real bug: the reply form header was showing the parent comment author's name and expertise because `FormWrapper` and `Form` fell back to `comment?.member` when the logged-in member had no name or expertise. Removing those fallbacks and the `comment` prop is the right core change, and the first new e2e test does fail on the base code for the reason it describes.

The PR also does three things beyond that fix, and two of them are problems. It crashes the main comment form by removing the optional chaining on `openForm`, even though `main-form.tsx` renders `FormWrapper` without an `openForm`. It changes `in_reply_to_id` in the reply submit to `parent.id`, which breaks reply-to-reply threading, since the backend silently drops the reference when it doesn't match the parent. It also changes the editor's editable gate from `name` to `expertise`, which is unexplained by the PR and makes the first new test likely to fail. I did not run the e2e suite; these conclusions come from reading the code and the backend service.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The removed optional chaining will throw a TypeError whenever the main comment box is focused or has content, which breaks the most common comment flow. The `in_reply_to_id` change silently discards reply-to-reply context. The editable-gate change is an unexplained behavior change that the new test appears to depend on in a way that will fail. The core fallback removal is sound and can ship once these are fixed.

architecture.overview:
Comment threads are rendered by `comment.tsx`. Each comment computes an `openForm` from the global `openCommentForms` state and renders a `ReplyFormBox` when a reply form is open for it. `ReplyForm` (`reply-form.tsx`) wraps the shared `Form` and `FormWrapper` from `forms/form.tsx`. `FormWrapper` renders the avatar and `FormHeader` (name and expertise) from the logged-in member, and reads `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` to decide padding and the "Reply to" line. The main comment box (`main-form.tsx`) reuses the same `FormWrapper` with no `openForm`. On submit, `addReply` posts to the comments API, and `comments-service.js` keeps `in_reply_to_id` only if the referenced comment belongs to the same parent.

The PR changes three things in this flow. First, the header now shows only the logged-in member's name and expertise, with no fallback to the parent comment's author. Second, the reply payload's `in_reply_to_id` is changed from `openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `parent.id`. Third, the editor's editable state is now gated on `member.expertise` instead of `member.name`. Each of these changes affects more than the header fix.
steps: Entry point: `comment.tsx` `openReplyForm` builds an `OpenCommentForm` with `in_reply_to_id` and `in_reply_to_snippet` only for replies to replies, and `ReplyFormBox` passes it to `ReplyForm`.

`reply-form.tsx` (changed): the submit handler now sends `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`, and the `FormWrapper` no longer receives `comment`. Confirm `parent` is the top-level comment when a reply-to-reply form is open.

`form.tsx` `FormWrapper` (changed): name and expertise come only from `member`. The `openForm` optional chaining was removed, which is unsafe because `main-form.tsx` renders this component without `openForm`.
`form.tsx` `Form` (changed): the editor is made editable only when `member.expertise` is set, not when `member.name` is set. This is the gate that decides whether the reply box accepts input.
Backend (unchanged): `comments-service.js` drops `in_reply_to_id` unless the referenced comment's `parent_id` matches the parent, so a wrong id is silently lost.
Tests (added): two e2e cases in `actions.test.ts` cover a member with no expertise and a member with no name. The first one depends on the editor being focusable, which the new gate affects.

findings.title: Main comment form crashes when focused because openForm is now dereferenced unguarded
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx`, `FormWrapper` (around line 313) reads `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without a guard. `MainForm` in `main-form.tsx` renders `FormWrapper` without an `openForm` prop, so focusing the main comment box throws a TypeError. Restore the optional chaining (`openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet`) so `FormWrapper` works when `openForm` is undefined. Keep the rest of this PR's change. Add or confirm an e2e case where the main comment box is focused.

findings.title: Reply-to-reply target is overwritten with the top-level parent id, so the reference is lost
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx` (around lines 27-35), the `addReply` payload was changed from `in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`. For reply-to-reply forms, `parent` is the top-level comment, so the backend's parent check in `ghost/core/core/server/services/comments/comments-service.js` (around line 361) drops the reference. Revert this line to `openForm.in_reply_to_id` and restore `openForm` in the `useCallback` dependency array. This change is not needed for the name and expertise fix.

findings.title: Editable gate switched from name to expertise, an unexplained behavior change
findings.body:
`editor.setEditable` used to depend on `memberName`, so the editor was locked only for members without a name. It now depends on `member?.expertise`.

This changes who can write a comment, and the PR description doesn't mention it:
- A logged-in member with a name but no expertise, which is allowed by the product, can no longer type into any comment form. Clicking the header calls `focusEditor`, which does nothing because `memberName` is set.
- A member with no name but with expertise becomes editable, which the old code blocked and the `focusEditor` comment ("Force to input a name first") tries to enforce.

The new effect also depends on the whole `member` object, so it re-runs on every member change.

::diff{file="apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx" lines="258-265"}

::callout{type="warning"}
If the intent is to require expertise before commenting, that is a product decision and needs its own PR description and tests. Otherwise restore the name-based gate and keep `[editor, memberName, progress]`.
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx`, the `useEffect` around line 264 changed `editor.setEditable(!!memberName && progress !== 'sending')` to `editor.setEditable(!!member?.expertise && progress !== 'sending')`. The PR goal is to stop showing the parent author's details and does not justify this change. Members with a name but no expertise can no longer type. Restore the name-based gate (`memberName`) and its dependency list. If expertise really should gate commenting, make that an explicit, separately-tested change.

findings.title: New expertise e2e test will time out because the editor is non-editable
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts` (test starting at line 614), the test 'Reply form does not inherit expertise from parent comment author' uses a member with `expertise: null`, and the `waitEditorFocused(editor)` call at line 639 expects the editor to be focused. With the current `setEditable(!!member?.expertise)` gate in `form.tsx`, the editor is not editable and won't take focus. Once the editable gate is decided (see the separate finding), either make this test's editor expectations match the chosen behavior, or remove the focus wait and assert only on the header, which is what the test verifies.

findings.title: Name-fallback test assertion is too weak to prove the header content
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts` (test starting at line 651, assertion around line 679), the name test asserts `not.toHaveText('Named Author')`, which passes for any other or missing text. `FormHeader` in `form.tsx` shows 'Anonymous' for a null name. Change the assertion to `toHaveText('Anonymous')` and keep the comment in sync with what the header shows.

findings.title: Unrelated class-order churn in reply-form.tsx
findings.body:
The wrapper `className` was reordered from `'mt-[-16px] pr-2'` to `'pr-2 mt-[-16px]'`. This is a cosmetic change that adds noise to a bug-fix diff. Drop it, or keep the original order to keep the diff focused.

::diff{file="apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx" lines="47-47"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx` around line 47, the wrapper div's className was reordered from `mt-[-16px] pr-2` to `pr-2 mt-[-16px]`. Revert to the original order so the diff contains only the intended fix.

findings.title: Removing the parent-author fallback is correct and well tested
findings.body:
The core of the PR is right. `FormWrapper` and `Form` no longer read `comment?.member`, and the `comment` prop was removed from `FormWrapper` and its only caller. `FormHeader` already renders `'Anonymous'` and `'Add your expertise'` as placeholders, so an empty member header now shows the right placeholder.

The first new e2e test fails on the base code, because the base shows the parent's expertise when the logged-in member has none. That makes it a true regression test for the reported bug.
